To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the tumour suppressor NKX3. 1 is a novel transcription factor regulating Prm3 and TPβ expression in prostate cancer; (ii) the transcription factor FOXP1 also regulates Prm3 and TBXA2R expression in prostate cancer, and (iii) the tumour promoter CpG island hypermethylation is associated with increased expression of the tumour suppressive TP isoform in PCa.
(1) The tumour suppressors NKX3. 1 and FOXP1 are key transcription factors regulating the expression of TPβ in the prostate cancer cell lines PC-3 and LnCaP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of TPα and/or TPβ expression in human cancer.
the identification of novel molecular targets for the development of more efficacious therapeutic agents in the treatment of prostate cancer.
the role of the TPα/β isoforms of the T Prostanoid Receptor in the pathogenesis of prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TPβ isoforms are regulated by FOXP1 and/or NKX3. 1 in prostate cancer.
TPβ is regulated by FOXP1 and/or NKX3.
TPα and TP β expression is regulated by FOXP1 and/or NKX3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TPβ is a key regulator of PCa progression, with its expression being tightly regulated by FOXP1 and the NKX3.

the transcriptional regulation of Prm3 and Prm1 by the tumour-suppressor NKX3.3 and the tumour-promoter FOXP1, respectively, provides a mechanism for the differential regulation of the TP isoforms in PCa.
TPβ expression is upregulated in PCa by a combination of CpG hypomethylation of Prm3 and transcriptional activation by FOXP1 and/or NKX3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FOXP1 and/or NKX3. 1 are likely to be important regulators of TP expression in prostate cancer.
